summary: The study describes a two-stage ALD process for depositing aluminum oxide (AlOx) on strong hydrophobic alkanethiolate self-assembled monolayers (SAMs). The first stage uses n-propanol as the oxygen source, while the second stage uses water. This process significantly improves the surface morphology of AlOx layers and maintains the structural integrity of the underlying SAMs.
evidence: Aluminum oxide (AlOx) was deposited onto strong hydrophobic surfaces of alkanethiolate self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) by a two-stage atomic layer deposition (ALD) process; the first stage utilized n-propanol as the oxygen source, and the second stage proceeded with water. The optimized two-step ALD process significantly improved the surface morphology of AlOx layers and effectively protected the structural integrities of underlying SAMs.
